references.text: After Adam and Eve ate from the tree of knowledge, they became aware of their nakedness and shame. This shows a direct contrast to their previous state of innocence and shamelessness in Genesis 2:25.
Adam tells God that he hid because he was naked, and God asks who told him so. This is the direct consequence of the loss of the shameless innocence described in 2:25.
Job says that he came naked from his mother's womb and naked shall he return. This connects to humanity's original nakedness as a natural state without shame.
Hebrews 4:13 speaks of all things being naked and exposed before God's eyes. In Genesis 2:25, Adam and Eve were naked without shame – they lived in complete openness toward God and each other.
